record.original_question: Describe the differential geometry of the Lie groupoid of multiphase or generalized volume-preserving diffeomorphisms equipped with its source-wise right-invariant L2 metric, including sectional curvature, Ricci curvature, and conjugate points, analogously to Arnold's description for D_mu(M).

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Describe the differential geometry (including computations of sectional and Ricci curvatures, conjugate points, etc.) for the right-invariant (source-wise) L2 -metric on the Lie groupoid of multiphase or generalized volume-preserving diffeomorphisms (analogous to Arnold’s description of the differential geometry of the group Dµ (M )). 4

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold equipped with a volume form $\mu$. Classically, Arnold showed that the Euler equations of an ideal incompressible fluid on $M$ describe the geodesic flow of the right-invariant $L^2$ metric on the group $D_\mu(M)$ of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$, and he developed the corresponding differential geometry (sectional curvatures, Ricci curvatures, conjugate points) of $D_\mu(M)$.

Consider now the Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ of multiphase (generalized) volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$: objects are measurable partitions (or, more generally, generalized configurations / Young-measure-like states) of $M$ preserving the total volume, and morphisms are diffeomorphism-like maps that intertwine such configurations while preserving the relevant volume forms. Equip $\mathcal{G}$ with the source-wise right-invariant $L^2$ metric, so that geodesics correspond to multiphase fluid flows (homogenized vortex sheets, generalized flows in the sense of Brenier, etc.).

Problem: Develop the differential geometry of $\mathcal{G}$ with respect to this source-wise right-invariant $L^2$ metric. Specifically:
(a) compute the sectional curvatures of $\mathcal{G}$ in terms of pairs of tangent vectors at identity bisections;
(b) compute the Ricci curvature in admissible directions;
(c) describe the locus and structure of conjugate points along geodesics,
in a manner analogous to Arnold's description for $D_\mu(M)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work (Izosimov–Khesin, "Geometry of generalized fluid flows", 2023) develops the variational/Hamiltonian framework for these groupoids and shows that multiphase fluids arise as geodesics of the source-wise right-invariant L² metric, but does not provide the curvature and conjugate-point analysis requested. Related curvature computations exist only for classical (single-phase) measure-preserving diffeomorphism groups (e.g., arXiv:2501.06599). No source was found carrying out Arnold-type curvature, Ricci, and conjugate-point computations on the multiphase groupoid itself, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of generalized fluid flows
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions of Euler equations are precisely the geodesics of an L² right-invariant (source-wise) metric on the corresponding Lie groupoids of multiphase volume-preserving diffeomorphisms.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the geodesic/groupoid framework but does not undertake the curvature/conjugate-point analysis.

status_evidence.title: Curvatures of measure-preserving diffeomorphism groups
status_evidence.snippet: Computes curvatures, their asymptotics and normalized Ricci curvatures for groups of measure-preserving diffeomorphisms (classical, single-phase setting).
status_evidence.claim: Curvature computations exist for the classical Arnold setting but not for the multiphase groupoid.
